text:
sarah.dev: getting 401 invalid_api_key when opening websocket to streams endpoint from a browser. REST calls with same key succeed. Example I tried: new WebSocket('wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams', 'Bearer rwd_ABC...') — browsers won't let me set Authorization header. any ideas?

alex.support: do you get a WS close frame or an http 401 during the handshake? can you paste the exact client error/logs (no secrets in public chat)

sarah.dev: browser console: "Failed to construct 'WebSocket': The subprotocol 'Bearer rwd_ABC...' is not allowed." then connection closes. network tab shows 101/upgrade attempt then immediate 401 response with body "invalid_api_key". node/ws with headers works fine (i.e. new WebSocket(url, { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer rwd_ABC...' } })) — so looks browser-specific.

alex.support: ok — browsers cannot set Authorization header on ws handshakes; people often pass token in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol subprotocol string (e.g. new WebSocket(url, 'Bearer <token>')). however some CDNs/proxies strip or normalize Sec-WebSocket-Protocol. do you have a CDN/edge in front of your app?

sarah.dev: yep we sit behind CloudFront. i also tried ?api_key=... on the wss url but CloudFront is removing the query on the upgrade, so same result.

alex.support: that matches what we've seen before — CloudFront/edge can drop Sec-WebSocket-Protocol or certain query params during websocket upgrades which leads to missing auth at the backend and a 401 invalid_api_key. two quick workarounds: 1) perform an HTTPS auth exchange from the browser to your backend: POST /session -> backend validates the Redwood key server-side and returns a short-lived session id/cookie the browser can use for the ws connection to your own proxy. 2) use our official JS SDK (it negotiates a short-lived handshake token over HTTPS then upgrades; this avoids sending long-lived keys from the browser).

sarah.dev: nice, thanks. is there anything you can check on your side (edge config) before i change our infra?

alex.support: we can check whether our ingress respects Sec-WebSocket-Protocol for your region, but because you're behind CloudFront it's likely happening at your CDN. quick test: from a node host (or curl+wscat) do a ws connect via your origin (bypass CF) — if that succeeds while the CloudFront-hosted one fails, CF is the culprit. if you'd like, DM me the origin and a timestamp and we'll ask edge team to inspect.

sarah.dev: i'll try bypassing CF and report back. thanks!

infra-bot: escalated to edge team for header/query param stripping investigation — ticket EDGE-2026 created.
